messages:
Alex: heads up — a customer consumed most of the org burst pool but only when targeting the 'gptx-verylarge' family. Others on the org are blocked. Thoughts on treating families differently?
Maria: is that the org-level burst pool or per-key?
Alex: org-level. single org hit ~180 credits on gptx-verylarge; org pool was 200 so left almost nothing. gptx-medium usage was fine.
Chris: cost perspective: verylarge is ~6x the base weight. if we keep absolute credits per family that will blow out cost exposure.
Tanya: UX note: console shows 1 bar for "burst credits" today. customers assume it's uniform. we should show a family breakdown and make the semantics explicit: "family-weighted consumption" or similar.
Kevin: implementation idea: maintain a single org pool, but compute effective_charge = tokens * family_weight. use family weighting to limit how many effective credits large models can take. e.g. weights {small:1, medium:2, large:6, verylarge:12}. then family_limit = floor(org_pool_base / weight).
Maria: edge case: what about requests that touch multiple models (routing fallback from verylarge->large) or toolchains that call multiple families? we should charge the sum of weighted tokens across models in the single request.
Alex: yes, request_weight = sum_over_segments(tokens_segment * weight(segment_model)). debit that from org_pool.
quota-bot: alert: org o-9812 surpassed soft-burst for family gptx-verylarge at 2026-06-15T09:24:11Z (usage_effective=184 > allowed=150) :warning:
Chris: we'll need telemetry metrics: tokens_by_family/min, effective_credits_consumed_by_family, overrides_used. Ops wants a per-family time series to drive autoscale and billing flags.
Tanya: console proposal: default shows org total + top-4 families by recent spend; expand to per-key and per-route panes; show a little "request weight" gauge per key. allow SREs to create timeboxed overrides (safelists) with audit trail.
Kevin: enforcement middleware sketch:
```
required = sum(tokens_by_model * weight[model])
if org_pool.try_take(required): allow
else if policy.allows_override(req): allow (tag=override)
else: respond 429 with header X-Quota-Remaining
```
We must emit an audit_event on overrides and include original_required + effective_charge for billing.
Maria: scheduled safelists are important — partner demo windows, load tests, etc. must auto-expire and be visible in audit logs. include actor, reason, expiration.
Alex: can we provide a "simulator" in dev console so customers can estimate how many bursts a given model mix will consume?
Tanya: yes, a small "how much will my demo cost" calculator would reduce support tickets.
Chris: billing: when override is used, produce a reconciliation event: {org, request_id, original_weight, charged_weight, override_id}. Also tag usage rows in raw telemetry so downstream ETL can compute invoice adjustments.
Kevin: dev note: add a "local-weight-mode" toggle so devs can test weighting logic without touching prod counters.
Alex: next steps: (1) RFC for family-weighted burst enforcement + API blueprint (2) Console mockups for family breakdown and safelist flow (3) POC middleware + unit tests for multi-model requests (4) telemetry spec for new metrics and override events. I'll start RFC.
quota-bot: created task Q-1022 to track RFC + POC.
Tanya: assigning UI mock to me. tagging @Kevin and @Maria for implementation + telemetry. sync Friday 10:30?
Kevin: I'll open a draft branch for the middleware and add tests for combined-model requests.
Maria: I'll draft telemetry events and schema. include sampling rate for debug-level override logs.
Alex: thanks — ping if you need anything. :+1:
